title: Agglomerative warmup scan notebook - microburst/warm-cache interplay
body:
Experiment goal:
- Understand how 'agglomerative priming' (multiple near-simultaneous short bursts that partially prime prefix KV cache) impacts tail latency during subsequent bursts.
- Find operational knobs (batch timeout, prefill window, kv-cache TTL, speculative scheduling) that reduce p99 without harming p50 or throughput.

Environment & baseline:
- Model: open-13B-quant-8bit (test container image: rwinf/model-open-13b:qa-2025-10-28)
- Hardware: mix of A100-80GB (primary), p4d for validation runs
- Runtime: redwood-serving v0.17.3 (local debug build with extra trace logs)
- Traffic generator: loadgen-v2 (Poisson/zipf modes), synthetic payloads (avg tokens 96, sd 40)
- Baseline config: concurrency_limit=12, batch_timeout_ms=8, kv_cache_enabled=true, kv_cache_ttl_ms=60000

Arrival patterns tested:
1) Single pulse: 300 concurrent reqs over 200ms (control)
2) Agglomerative pulses: 3 pulses spaced 400ms apart, each 120 concurrent reqs, repeat every 10s (primary)
3) Steady high: 150 sustained qps (to compare steady-state)
4) Interleaved cold: alternating cold (no KV) and warm requests to simulate mixed tenants

Key metrics captured:
- p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) per-window (10s windows)
- tokens/s per GPU
- kv_cache_hit_rate (sampled at 1s)
- batch_size distribution (mean, 95th)
- queueing depth (per-inference thread)

Results (quick numbers, approximate):
- Baseline single pulse: p50=42ms, p95=110ms, p99=210ms, tokens/s=38k
- Agglomerative pulses (same baseline config): p50=46ms, p95=140ms, p99=420ms (!) -> big p99 tail after second pulse in sequence
- KV hit rate during agglomerative pulses: 72% avg (drops to 55% immediately after spike due to eviction window)
- Observed backlog: small queues spike to 18 requests, batching collapsed into a few large batches (mean batch_size=18 -> causing kernel sync pauses)

What I think is happening:
- Partial priming: early pulses populate some KV entries but not enough to get high hit rates for all common prefixes. Later pulses read mostly warm-ish prefixes causing uneven KV cache locality.
- Large batches created by simultaneous arrivals cause a small number of long-running GPU kernel calls which increases scheduling head-of-line blocking for following requests.
- Eviction/TTL interplay: TTL of 60s is fine normally, but the working set of the synthetic workload is right at the eviction threshold, so bursts push some entries out and then immediate re-reads cause extra cache misses mid-burst -> p99 spikes.

Quick interventions tested (short runs):
A) Lower batch_timeout_ms to 4ms -> effect: p50 marginally up (~+3ms), p95 down (~-20ms), p99 down (~-90ms) for agglomerative pulses. Throughput drops ~6%.
B) Prefill speculative requests: on pulse start, schedule a speculative 2-token warmup call (cheap) for top-k prefixes -> p99 reduced ~-120ms but overhead increased tokens/s by 4%. Complex to implement for multi-tenant.
C) Increase kv_cache_ttl_ms to 180000 -> hit_rate up to 88%, p99 reduced to ~230ms, throughput unchanged. Risk: memory usage growth on long runs.
D) Soft-priority lanes: mark speculative warmups as low priority so they don't take GPU slots away from real requests -> mixed results in fairness tests.

Micro-observation logs (timestamps UTC):
- 2025-11-03T15:22:11 - first agglomerative run: p99 jumped at +420ms 2.1s after first pulse. Traces show long kernel on batch id 4123.
- 2025-11-03T15:24:40 - lowered batch_timeout to 4ms, run 5 repeats: median p99 decreased but some runs still show sporadic 300-350ms spikes aligned with GC cycles on host (need to correlate).
- 2025-11-04T09:03:02 - kv_ttl increased, memory resident per-GPU +8%, hit-rate much smoother across windows.

ASCII mini-plot (p99 over time for one run; time windows 10s):
[ 100, 110, 130, 290, 420, 210, 180, 140, 120 ] -> spike in middle aligns with second/third pulse overlap

Open hypotheses / next experiments:
- Hypothesis 1: kernel serialization by large batches amplifies tail when KV hit-rate is patchy. Test by forcing max_batch_size=8 and measuring p99.
- Hypothesis 2: small background warmup ops timed precisely before predicted microburst reduce tail with lower cost than increasing TTL. Need ramp-based scheduler (pre-schedule warmup 50ms before expected pulse).
- Hypothesis 3: host-level GC/maintenance correlates with residual spikes; schedule stress runs across different host images to isolate.

Short to-do (actionable):
- [ ] Run controlled max_batch_size=8 sweep (10 repeats) across A100 and p4d. (owner: Micah)
- [ ] Add 2-minute memory/time series for kv_cache_evictions to telemetry (owner: Ivy)
- [ ] Draft a small proposal for speculative prefill with a cost model (owner: Rafi)
- [ ] Add correlation traces between host GC events and p99 windows (owner: Micah)

Notes to self:
- Keep synthetic payload realistic (avg 96 tokens) — shorter payloads reduce batch formation and change dynamics.
- When sharing, include a short replay script and the loadgen seed.

Attachments (local): loadgen-seed-20251103.txt, run-logs/agglomerative-20251103-t1.json (will upload to GH gist later).

Concluding quick thought:
- Cheapest immediate lever: reduce batch_timeout slightly (from 8ms -> 4ms) to collapse the big batch formation. Best engineering trade currently is TTL increase but riskier for long runs. Prefill/speculative looks promising but needs cost accounting.

-- Micah
